physics_goals.quote: RNO-G will be the first production-scale radio detector for in-ice neutrino signals
physics_goals.value: Detect ultra-high-energy (PeV-scale and above) astrophysical and cosmogenic neutrinos using in-ice radio detection at the top of the Greenland ice sheet

summary.plain: A radio-antenna neutrino detector being built into the ice at the very top of Greenland's ice sheet, one station at a time, to catch the radio flash from the highest-energy neutrinos from space.
summary.technical: In-ice radio neutrino detector under phased construction at Summit Station, Greenland (72°35'46"N 38°25'19"W, atop >3 km of ice); design target 35 stations on a 1.25 km grid, each with three boreholes (~100 m deep) holding 15 receiving antennas in total plus 9 near-surface antennas. 7 stations deployed over the 2021-2022 field seasons; deployment paused in 2023 to evaluate instrument performance before continuing.
